transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Vanguard Head of Platform), Priya Patel (Vanguard Security), Carlos Ruiz (Vanguard CTO)

Summary (auto): quick intake on KMS/SSO gating, retention needs, and whether Vanguard should use Hosted vs Dedicated. Agreement to share SOC2 docs and schedule technical bench in two weeks.

[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Hey team, thanks for making time — um — appreciate it. Today our goal is to run through your security gates around keys, SSO, retention and which hosting mode makes sense. Maya will handle the technical bits.
[00:18] Liam Chen: Thanks Jamie. Quick note — we're trying to finalize a vendor that can meet our compliance bar (SOC2 + ISO27001 ideally) and also let us manage keys. Primary blockers are KMS control, audit logs, and SAML flows.
[00:32] Maya Singh: Got it. We'll cover how Redwood supports customer-managed keys, audit log retention, RBAC and SAML/SCIM. Quick clarifying q: do you expect HSM-backed keys or will cloud KMS be OK?
[00:46] Priya Patel: HSM preferred for now for the pilot. We run regulated workloads — payments metadata — and security wants to see key attestations or HSM integration.
[01:05] Jamie Ortega: We support both — Hosted with customer-managed KMS keys (Cloud KMS) and Private deployments with HSM options for on-prem or VPC. For Dedicated we can surface the KMS integration too. There are some differences I can outline.
[01:28] Carlos Ruiz: Walk me through the differences re: audit logs and retention. We need at least three years of immutable audit logs and fine-grained event logs for token usage.
[01:44] Maya Singh: Right. On Hosted we provide detailed request-level audit trails — token usage, model, route — retained for X days by default, with add-on retention up to a year. For customers needing multi-year retention we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs can be shipped to your logging stack or exported to your S3 with immutability controls.
[02:12] Priya Patel: When you say "request-level" are you including prompt content? Our policy excludes storing PII prompts in cleartext.
[02:25] Maya Singh: By default we redact user-submitted PII from logs; we also offer policy-based masking. For Private/Dedicated you can configure retention and disable content-level persistence entirely — just metadata and hashes. Note: we sometimes call this prefix cache/kv cache logs, spelled out differently in our docs, so apologies if names are fuzzy in the recordings.
[02:52] Liam Chen: Ok. SOC2 — do you have a current report? We need the type II and the date range.
[03:02] Jamie Ortega: Yes. We have a SOC2 Type II from late 2025 and an ISO attestation in progress. I'll share the SOC2 summary and the auditor letter after the call.
[03:14] Carlos Ruiz: Good. On SAML and SCIM — our IdP is Okta. We want SSO, SAML assertions, groups provisioning and attribute mapping for RBAC. Any known gaps?
[03:27] Maya Singh: Okta is on our supported list. We do SAML and SCIM for group sync. There are a few things to watch: SCIM delta sync timing, group scoping so you don't over-provision, and attribute mapping semantics — we give a sample mapping file.
[03:45] Priya Patel: Do you support enforced session timeouts based on SAML attributes?
[03:50] Maya Singh: We can read SAML session attributes and map to session controls; for Hosted we have session TTL controls and for Dedicated/Private you can enforce via your IdP or local auth layer. We'll show the SAML metadata and example assertion during the technical deep-dive.
[04:08] Liam Chen: About KMS — we currently run with GCP KMS and an internal HSM for very sensitive keys. Does Redwood integrate with Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) workflows?
[04:22] Jamie Ortega: Yes — BYOK is supported. Hosted customers can bring cloud-managed keys and we do envelope encryption; for full HSM-backed BYOK and attestations we'd route you to Private or Dedicated with HSM connectors. There's a handshake and rotation policy we document.
[04:40] Carlos Ruiz: And rotation — automatic or manual? We require rotation that we can trigger and have audit records for.
[04:47] Maya Singh: Rotation can be automated or manual. We keep a rotation log and can forward key rotation events to your audit stream. For Hosted we record rotation events in our admin audit logs; Dedicated/Private allows you to control the KMS endpoints so rotations are entirely in your control.
[05:05] Priya Patel: What about secrets in transit — TLS versions, mTLS?
[05:11] Maya Singh: We use TLS1.2+ and support TLS1.3. mTLS for internal control plane-to-runtime is available in Private deployments; optional mTLS for customer-facing endpoints can be arranged in Dedicated.
[05:25] Liam Chen: Latency vs encryption tradeoff — some of our teams worry that additional encryption layers/extra routing to KMS will add token-level latency. Any benchmark data?
[05:38] Maya Singh: Good question. For Hosted with cloud KMS envelope keys there is a small one-time cost when material is unwrapped. We typically see sub-10ms per-request for key operations when cached — worst case cold unwrap is higher. For Dedicated we can deploy regional KMS instances to minimize round trip. We'll include latency profiles with the Dedicated pricing doc.
[05:58] Carlos Ruiz: Are there any limitations on model tuning or quantization when using Private/HSM setups?
[06:05] Maya Singh: No hard limitations. The runtime will run the same models; quantization and kernel selection are orthogonal; the main constraints are networking and storage encryption for large model artifacts.
[06:20] Jamie Ortega: Quick pause — I know this is a lot — let me ask the procurement-ish question: what's your expected timeline and must-have gates?
[06:29] Liam Chen: Ideally a pilot in May, production by Q3. Must-haves: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO with Okta, HSM-backed keys for prod, 3-year audit log retention or exportability, and RBAC tied to groups.
[06:45] Priya Patel: Also we'll run a security questionnaire (vendor risk) — we typically need answers plus supporting evidence.
[06:52] Jamie Ortega: We do vendor questionnaires regularly; I can attach a completed version for a similar customer, and we'll provide evidence where allowed (redacted).
[07:03] Maya Singh: For the questionnaire items about data retention and deletion: Hosted has configurable TTLs; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to zero for content. We also offer a compliance mode that disables persistent KV cache for sensitive routes.
[07:27] Liam Chen: How granular is RBAC? Can we create per-environment roles and lock write to production model routes?
[07:36] Maya Singh: Yes — per-route RBAC, team-level roles (admin/editor/viewer), and token scoping. For Dedicated/Private you can sync groups from SCIM and enforce environment labels.
[07:48] Carlos Ruiz: Do you have an approval flow or can we wire up our CI to auto-approve model rollouts?
[07:54] Maya Singh: We support canary rollouts and A/B policies; approval hooks can be integrated via API/webhooks into your CI.
[08:05] Priya Patel: On retention exports — you mentioned exporting logs to S3. Are these encrypted server-side or client-side? Can we hook into our own KMS?
[08:16] Maya Singh: Exported logs can be encrypted server-side with your KMS or client-side before upload. For Dedicated/Private you can point exports at your S3 with your SSE-KMS keys.
[08:29] Liam Chen: Any incident response playbook? If there's a suspected key compromise, what's the workflow?
[08:36] Jamie Ortega: We have an IR runbook: immediate key rotation, isolation of affected nodes, customer notification SLA (usually 1 hour for critical incidents), and post-incident report. For Dedicated/Private we can agree to shorter SLAs contractually.
[08:55] Carlos Ruiz: The 1-hour SLA for notification — is that written down in your standard terms?
[09:01] Jamie Ortega: For Hosted that's our operational target; Dedicated customers can include tightened notification and response SLAs in their contract. We'll surface the exact wording in the SLA attachment.
[09:12] Priya Patel: About auditability — can we run ad-hoc queries against your logs or do you provide a view only?
[09:20] Maya Singh: We provide both. Hosted customers get a queryable logs UI with exports; Dedicated/Private customers can ingest the logs into their SIEM for ad-hoc queries and long-term retention.
[09:34] Liam Chen: For compliance, we also need a data flow diagram that shows where model context, KV cache, and logs live. Can you provide that?
[09:42] Jamie Ortega: Yes — Maya will attach a data flow diagram and note the default retention points and masking behaviors.
[09:50] Maya Singh: I'll attach two versions: Hosted default and Dedicated/Private with BYOK/HSM.
[09:59] Carlos Ruiz: Regarding legal — do you terminate and delete data on contract end? We have retention rules to avoid holding customer content beyond N days unless legally required.
[10:10] Jamie Ortega: Yes, we support data deletion on contract termination. We provide certs of deletion for Dedicated/Private when we're responsible for the data store. For Hosted we'll coordinate export and deletion processes; some artifacts (billing) persist as required.
[10:28] Priya Patel: Are there any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
[10:33] Jamie Ortega: We have a subprocessors list; some cloud infra providers and monitoring vendors are listed. I'll include the latest subprocessors PDF.
[10:41] Liam Chen: On the encryption side — are keys ever persisted in plaintext on disk on your side?
[10:47] Maya Singh: No. Keys are either in your KMS or wrapped. We use envelope encryption; plaintext material is not persisted. For Private installs you control the key endpoints.
[10:58] Carlos Ruiz: One last technical point — does Redwood's runtime cache KV data across requests in a way that could leak between tenants?
[11:07] Maya Singh: No cross-tenant leakage. We logically isolate caches per-tenant and have memory scrubbing and TTLs to reduce risk. In Dedicated we can also configure physical isolation.
[11:19] Liam Chen: Alright. Sounds promising. Let's talk procurement blockers: we need a completed security questionnaire, SOC2 doc, pricing for Dedicated pilot and production, and an Okta SAML test.
[11:29] Jamie Ortega: We'll deliver the SOC2 and questionnaire answers, plus the SAML metadata and sample test plan. We'll also prepare Dedicated pilot pricing and a proposed benchmark week.
[11:38] Priya Patel: For the benchmark week — we'll want a small test harness hitting the inference endpoints with masked test prompts and measure P95 latency, token costs and verify logs shape.
[11:46] Maya Singh: Perfect — we'll provide a test harness repo and a sample traffic generator. For the harness we'll also include guidance on masking and what to exclude so you don't leak PII into logs.
[11:57] Carlos Ruiz: Who should we contact for legal and procurement?
[12:00] Jamie Ortega: I'll be primary AE contact, and our sales ops/legal liaison is Rebecca Holt — I'll include her in the thread.
[12:09] Liam Chen: Ok great. Any outstanding concerns from Redwood side?
[12:12] Maya Singh: One thing — for production HSM-linked workloads we'll likely need a short proof of concept to validate rotation workflows and latency; it's standard.
[12:21] Priya Patel: That's fine. We'll run a POC.
[12:24] Jamie Ortega: Great — recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 and subprocessors, Maya sends SAML/SCIM docs and test harness, you (Priya) provide IAM diagram and retention policy, Carlos to confirm budget/regional preference. We'll target the technical deep-dive and bench on 2026-04-22.
[12:41] Liam Chen: Sounds good, thanks all.
[12:43] Carlos Ruiz: Thanks.
[12:44] Priya Patel: Thank you.
[12:45] Jamie Ortega: Thanks — I'll follow up with the items.
